description:
Zoox is looking for an embedded software engineer to build out simulation infrastructure for our firmware. Our firmware runs on many ECUs across the robot, including the components that drive, brake, steer, and monitor the vehicle's health. Today, most of that firmware depends on hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches, which are expensive, hard to scale, and slow to iterate on. You will build the simulation capabilities that let firmware run in virtualized, software-in-the-loop (SIL), and hybrid SIL/HIL environments, integrated with Zoox's core simulation platform and the pipelines the rest of the autonomy stack already uses.
You'll be one of the first engineers on a new embedded-focused simulation team within the Firmware organization: simulation infrastructure engineering, built by and for firmware. The work you do here will lay the groundwork for Firmware's adoption of Zoox's simulation and more advanced test platform infrastructure. It spans much of the embedded stack, from low-level BSPs, through middleware such as messaging, HALs, and OSALs, up to the application layer. You'll need to understand what embedded software optimizes for (determinism, timing, resource limits, hardware interfaces) and turn that into simulation infrastructure that firmware teams trust and adopt.


In this role, you will: 
 

 
 Build out simulation infrastructure for Zoox's embedded platforms, filling the gaps in Zoox's simulation stack that keep firmware from adopting it



 
 Virtualize embedded platforms across the stack, from BSPs and HAL/OSAL layers to messaging middleware and peripherals, so firmware can run without target hardware



 
 Develop and extend SIL environments that integrate firmware with Zoox's core simulation platform and pipelines



 
 Support and evolve hybrid SIL/HIL test platforms that combine real hardware with simulated components



 
 Partner with Zoox's simulation, HIL, and firmware feature teams to adapt existing firmware for simulation and reduce the Firmware org's reliance on HIL






Qualifications
 

 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or equivalent experience



 
 1–3 years of experience developing simulation infrastructure or embedded software for real-time systems



 
 Strong C/C++ and Python programming skills



 
 Understanding of embedded fundamentals: RTOS concepts, interrupts and timing, memory-constrained systems, and hardware/peripheral interfaces



 
 Experience building simulation, emulation, or virtualization environments for embedded systems (e.g., SIL, QEMU, Renode, hardware/peripheral models)






Bonus Qualifications
 

 
 Experience with QNX, SafeRTOS, FreeRTOS, or similar embedded operating systems



 
 Familiarity with automotive communication protocols (CAN, LIN, Ethernet) and how to model or bridge them in simulation



 
 Hands-on experience with HIL systems or hybrid SIL/HIL test setups






Compensation
There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.
 
Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.
